title: What AI actually does
summary: Separate rules, learned predictions, and generated content before choosing a tool.
objectives: Frame a task as inputs and outputs

sections.title: Start with a decision
paragraphs: An AI system transforms inputs into an output that helps someone decide or act. A classifier assigns a category, a regressor estimates a number, and a generative model produces a sequence such as text. None of these outputs is automatically true merely because a model produced it. Define the decision before choosing a model.

Consider sorting support messages. A keyword rule is easy to inspect, but misses unfamiliar wording. A learned classifier can use patterns from labeled examples. A language model can write a reply, but needs a separate check that the reply answers the actual question. These are different tasks with different failure costs.

sections.title: Learning is not using
paragraphs: Training adjusts model parameters using examples and an objective. Inference uses the resulting parameters on an input. Retrieving a document or adding text to a prompt does not, by itself, update those parameters.

Start with a simple baseline and a small set of representative examples. Record correct answers and difficult cases. A more elaborate model earns its place by improving the outcome under the same evaluation, including latency and operating cost.

code.explanation: This baseline uses explicit rules. There is no training step, probability estimate, or external model call. It creates something concrete to compare against.

practice.goal: Discover the limits of a rule-based classifier.
steps: Add six messages with known categories.
Include a synonym and a message mentioning both categories.
Count correct predictions and document the two hardest failures.
practice.solution: A message about a receipt may require billing but miss the invoice rule. A message with both keywords takes the first branch. Add a review category for ambiguity instead of silently treating the first match as certain.
practice.expected: The initial script prints account, billing, then review. Your expanded set should expose at least one limitation.

quiz.question: Which action changes learned model parameters?
quiz.explanation: Training updates parameters. Inference and retrieval can change the information used for an answer without retraining the model.
